summary: A whole map-and-list screen from data: places as numbered markers on a map (WorldMap, framed to fit them or a given region) and the same places as a list (a number, a name, a detail, a distance or rating). On a phone or a tall window the map is on top (about 42% of the height) and the list under it; on a wide window (from 600 dp and landscape) the list is a side panel on the left (280 to 360 dp) and the map fills the rest. Tapping a row selects it and enlarges its marker; tapping a marker selects its row.

items.doc: One object per place: {"title", "subtitle", "meta", "metaIcon", "place", "label"}. title (the name) and place are required: place is a city name (Natural Earth's 1,250 places: capitals, state capitals, large cities) or "lon,lat" as one string ("2.2945,48.8584"; not an array). subtitle is the second line (an address, opening hours, a category), meta the value at the row's end ("1.2 km", "4.6"), metaIcon an icon before it ("star", "schedule", "directions_walk"). label replaces the row's spoken text

title.doc: The list's heading ("Stores"); omit for no header

subtitle.doc: A line under the heading ("6 within 10 km")

selected.doc: The selected place, from 0. Bind a resources variable ("@sel") to preset or read it. Do not name it step

region.doc: Frame this region instead of fitting the places: a continent ("Europe"), a subregion, a country ("FRA") or [lonMin, latMin, lonMax, latMax]. Omit to frame the places tightly (the default, and usually best)

borders.doc: Draw country borders (false: plain land). Worth it for places across several countries; a world of borders at medium detail costs ~40 KB

states.doc: Draw state or province borders of these countries (ISO A3: USA, CAN, AUS, DEU, ...), as WorldMap states: inside one big country they are what gives the map its landmarks

sea.doc: Sea fill (none by default: mapBackground shows)

mapBackground.doc: Behind the map (the sea when sea is not given)

markerColor.doc: Markers, the row numbers and the selected row's bar

label.doc: The map's accessibility label ("Map of six stores in Paris")

hit.doc: Half the side in dp of a marker's tap square

mapShare.doc: The map's least share of the height under the header when stacked; it grows into height the rows leave empty (up to 0.9:1)

wideAt.doc: Width in dp from which a landscape window puts the list beside the map

width.doc: The width it has, when it is not the whole window

headerEnd.doc: At the end of the header: an IconButton (filter, search) or a Badge

pitfalls: Give places as data and let it decide: under wideAt (600 dp), or when the window is not clearly landscape (width under 1.2 x height, a portrait tablet), the header, the map (mapShare of the height under it) and the list stack; otherwise the list is a side panel (38% of the width, 280 to 360 dp) and the map fills the rest. Decided by the window, never by content

place is a city name from Natural Earth's 1,250 places (capitals, state capitals, large cities; the error names a missing one) or "lon,lat" as ONE string ("12.57,55.68"). An array [lon, lat] is flattened by the expander and fails

The map frames the places tightly (WorldMap fit) at every size; markers are 22 dp discs, so places closer than about 30 dp on the smallest map overlap: on a phone a 360 dp wide map, so keep places at least ~1/12 of the frame's width apart. There is no street or city-level map: pick places a world or continent map can show (cities, stores across a country or continent, offices worldwide, a road trip's stops), not shops in one town

Rows and markers share one selected variable (from 0): a row tap selects, a marker tap (within hit dp of it) selects its row, highlighted with a tint and a bar. The list does not scroll to a marker's row; with more rows than fit, the selected row can be off screen on a phone

Each marker is its place's number (from 1), the same number leading its row. Rows are 64 dp with a subtitle, 52 without; title and subtitle are one line each (ellipsized), meta (a distance, a rating, a time) is not cut: keep it short

Bytes: the map geometry dominates (a world of land at low detail ~6 KB, Europe with borders ~10 KB, a world with borders at medium ~40 KB), then about 1.4 KB per place (its row, its marker in both panes, its tap test). The map is written twice (stacked and side panes, one shown); its path is one shared resource

Marker taps run on the map canvas's touch down (touchX/touchY against each marker), so they work where the marker is drawn in all players; rows are ordinary clicks with a spoken label (title, subtitle, meta)

A worldwide set of places frames the whole world, which cannot fill a square or tall box: the stacked map's height is capped at the frame's own aspect, but a side pane on a squarish window shows empty sea above and below. Places within a continent or a country fill every size; use detail medium when the frame is one region (a few states), where low detail shows crude coasts
width and height default to the window: pass them when it is not the whole window. The list sits on surface (background), the map on mapBackground; land is track
